title: Even without self-commendation, no rival divine word appears — duty stops at what God revealed
source_text: L. Sed quamvis Scriptura sacra nullam traditionum mentionem faceret, nec propriam perfectionem & sufficientiam ullibi commendaret, nihilominus vere nec sine ratione affirmaremus, nullum esse verbum Dei non scriptum: quia nullum tale comparet, & traditio quae tanquam divina proponitur habet in se notas quibus agnoscitur humana esse, & argumenta quae convincunt illam non esse satis tutum fidei fundamentum, quemadmodum superiori disputatione a nobis ostensum est. Nam sicut verum Dei verbum, & legitima fidei principia non opus habent probari alio Dei verbo, & deduci ex aliis fidei principiis, sed fidelibus innotescunt ex signis & notis innitis, aliisque argumentis & credendi motivis, ita etiam, ut merito rejiciamus id, quod falso ut Dei verbum proponitur, & legitimum fidei principium, non opus est expresso aliquo testimonio, quod desumptum sit ex vero Dei verbo, sed satis est ut in se habeat indicia & notas imbecillitatis humanae, & desint motiva atque argumenta quibus sufficienter fideles moveri & suaderi possint, ut illud tanquam divinum suscipiant. Ex eo vero quod praeter Scripturam nullum aliud extat & comparet Dei verbum, evidenter deducitur illam necessaria omnia continere. Nam per se notum est, homines de rebus divinis & supernaturalibus non teneri plura scire & credere, quam Deo placuit ipsis revelare & manifestare.
pass_a_gloss: But even if sacred Scripture made no mention of traditions, and nowhere commended its own perfection and sufficiency, nevertheless we would truly and not without reason affirm that there is no unwritten word of God: because no such thing appears, and the tradition that is proposed as divine has in itself notes by which it is recognized to be human, and arguments that convince that it is not a sufficiently safe foundation of faith, as was shown by us in the preceding disputation. For just as the true word of God and the legitimate principles of faith do not need to be proved by another word of God and deduced from other principles of faith, but become known to the faithful from innate signs and notes, and from other arguments and motives of believing, so also, that we may rightly reject that which is falsely proposed as the word of God and a legitimate principle of faith, there is no need of some express testimony taken from the true word of God, but it is enough that it have in itself marks and notes of human weakness, and that motives and arguments be wanting by which the faithful can be sufficiently moved and persuaded to receive it as divine. But from this, that besides Scripture no other word of God exists and appears, it is evidently deduced that it contains all things necessary. For it is known of itself that men are not bound to know and believe more about divine and supernatural things than it has pleased God to reveal and manifest to them.
pass_b_english: Even if Scripture never named traditions or praised its own sufficiency, we would still deny an unwritten word of God.
No such word appears; proposed divine tradition carries human marks and fails as a safe faith-foundation.
True first principles need no higher proof — and false claimants need no express biblical rebuttal if their weakness is plain.
Since no other divine word exists beside Scripture, it holds all that is necessary: men owe no more belief than God has revealed.
